Keywords: Religious eccentricity and care of the poor
RagShortTexts: Unusual conduct may carry religious criticism.
Poor or troubled people still require care and judgment.

Variants.Content: Some express devotion through austerity, begging or perplexing conduct; others are displaced by poverty or illness. Responses range from respect to suspicion. Clergy and kin consider conduct and circumstances; striking words do not replace care or guarantee prophecy.
Guards avoid injury and assess whether a distressed stranger needs food or kin. Treating every cry as intelligence or spying distracts from real threats.
Authorities seek clergy and witnesses before punishment. Tolerating religious criticism differs from abandoning order; alms cannot make one striking figure carry a town’s unmet needs.
Neighbors differ over holiness and distress. A meal is easier to provide than shelter and sustained care, usually borne by family and nearby households.
